transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Could you start by telling me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I've just been waking up with this really heavy, hollow sadness. I'm a dancer, and lately it's... it's kind of like the studio lights are on, but there’s just no music in me anymore. I just feel really down, and I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
How long have you been feeling this way—waking up with this heavy, hollow sadness?
Um, I'd say it's been about nine months. Yeah, this depressed feeling has been going on for around nine months now.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it felt good at the time?

Yeah, actually, I have. Um, there were these stretches where I just felt... dazzlingly alive. Like I had all this incredible energy. But it wasn't always just feeling good. I would get suddenly furious if anyone questioned my plans or, you know, reminded me that my ankle still needed rest. So, yes, I've definitely had periods like what you're describing.
During those periods of high energy and irritability, how many days in a row did that typically last?

Um, I'm not entirely sure exactly how many days in a row it would last. I didn't really keep track of the time when it was happening. It was definitely a few days, but I couldn't give you a specific number.

During that period of high energy and irritability, did it cause serious problems in your dancing, relationships, or daily life—like missing rehearsals, conflicts with others, or needing to be hospitalized—or were you still able to function fairly normally?

Well, it definitely caused problems. I mean, I wasn't hospitalized or anything, but... I fell way behind on my teaching prep. I also completely missed a grant deadline for my choreography work, which was a big deal. The studio just got so chaotic that the people I collaborate with had to step in and start handling basic scheduling for me because I just wasn't doing it. I was still showing up for the absolute essentials, like teaching my actual classes, but I definitely wasn't functioning the way I normally do.
During this past nine months of feeling down, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

No, I haven't. I mean, it's been a really hard nine months, and I've felt incredibly low and unmotivated, but... I've never thought about hurting myself or wanting to end things. It hasn't gotten to that point.

During these past nine months of feeling down, has the depression been severe enough to significantly interfere with your ability to teach, choreograph, or carry out your daily responsibilities, or have you still been able to manage most of your usual activities?

Well, it's actually a lot like what happened during that high-energy time I mentioned earlier. The depression has definitely interfered. I've fallen way behind on my teaching prep again, and I completely missed another grant deadline for my choreography. The studio has gotten really disorganized, to the point where my collaborators have had to step in and handle the basic scheduling for me. I'm still managing to show up for the absolute essentials, like teaching my classes, but I'm just not functioning the way I normally do.
During these past nine months, have you noticed significant trouble concentrating or making decisions, or persistent feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt?

I haven't really had trouble concentrating, but... the guilt has been pretty heavy. I keep replaying those cancelled performances in my head. I just keep telling myself that I let everyone down—the dancers, the funders, the whole community. People have actually been a lot kinder about it than I deserve, but I just can't shake this feeling that I'm completely worthless for letting it all fall apart.

During these past nine months of feeling depressed, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or having beliefs that others found unusual or not based in reality?

No, not during these past nine months. Um, those mountain messages and that humming voice I experienced... that really only happened during that wired stretch when I was barely sleeping and racing through all my plans. Since my mood dropped, I mean, I still feel guilty and really slowed down, but I haven't heard the voice again, and I haven't believed that any signs were directing me. It's just been the depression.
